newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 14.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Traders who hoped the market would establish a clear direction this week were disappointed, Random Lengths said. Instead, prices backed and filled as dealers replaced sparingly and mills resisted cutting prices, confident trading will revive as weather improves, the reporting agency said.

Some prices firmed or rose early in the week based on last week's late flurry. A few cracks showed up in specific items toward the end of the week but didn't develop into a full-fledged price retreat, Random Lengths said.
Trading favored sellers who could ship quickly, whether from mills or distribution facilities. Dealers, fearing prices could not hold current levels, shopped secondaries hard for fill-ins.

Though inventories at secondaries reportedly leaned to the heavy side in the Upper Midwest, stocks were modest to light in may other areas, the agency said. Wholesalers stayed frustrated by an inability to maneuver on either side of the market.

But wholesalers usually found buyers for wood they owned. Poor weather in parts of the South cut into consumption but also worsened log shortages. Continued mild temperatures in the Northeast caused traders to wonder if some jobs now under way have been borrowed from spring business. The big CLA meeting in Montreal cut into trading in eastern areas, the agency said.

Word from more Canadian producers that they had filled their allotments of fee-free and $50 wood for the U.S. didn't stir buyers, weary of the subject. Canadian exports as of February 6 were 37.6 percent of quarterly January-March fee-free quota and 89.6 pct of the annual April-March quota, the agency said.

A mixed performance in dimension and studs resulted in only a $1 gain for the composite framing index. Meanwhile, price of 12-inch boards in several species continued to climb into uncharted territory. Southern Pine timbers and radius edge decking remained hot sellers and the price of Premium decking hit a new high.
